baseline: Host LTP 20260529 prebuilt (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/statfs03): passed 1, failed 0, broken 0, skipped 0. Per step, what a correct kernel returns: (1) setup mkdir("testdir", 0444) as root in the 0700 root-owned tmpdir -> 0. (2) setup mkdir("testdir/subdir", 0444) as root, creating an entry inside the mode-0444 root-owned "testdir" -> 0, because CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE grants MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC on a *directory* unconditionally, with no execute bit required anywhere in the mode. (3) seteuid(nobody) -> 0, fsuid follows euid and the effective capability set is cleared. (4) the one real assertion, statfs03.c:36 TST_EXP_FAIL(statfs("testdir/subdir", &buf), EACCES) as nobody -> -1/EACCES(13), because search permission (MAY_EXEC) on the path prefix "testdir" is denied: nobody is neither owner nor group, and the other bits of 0444 are r--. So the test asserts an EACCES that must come from the *unprivileged* lookup, while every root-side setup step must succeed.
failing_assertion: The assertion is never reached. Asterinas dies in setup one line earlier: `statfs03.c:26: TBROK: mkdir(testdir/subdir, 0444) failed: EACCES (13)` (kirk verbose, ramfs tmpdir). mkdir returns EACCES where Linux returns 0. Kirk result: Passed 0, Failed 0, Broken 1, Skipped 0 vs host 1/0/0/0. statfs03.c:36 never executes, so the statfs behaviour the test exists to check is untested rather than wrong.
root_cause: In the default `Inode::check_permission` (kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:573-628) the CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE branch at 585-604 first subtracts MAY_READ|MAY_WRITE at line 588, then at 590-603 applies the rule "executable DACs are overridable when there is at least one exec bit set" to *every* inode type. Directories are never exempted. mkdir("testdir/subdir") reaches Path::check_dir_entry_mutation (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:265-269), which asks for MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC on the parent "testdir". For root: has_dac_override_capability (inode.rs:631-640) is true, so perm reduces to MAY_EXEC alone; perm.may_exec() is true at 591; "testdir" is mode 0444 so is_owner_executable / is_group_executable / is_other_executable (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_attr/mode.rs:45,57,69) are all false; and line 598 returns EACCES before the owner/group/other mode checks at 606-625 are ever consulted. The defect is exactly the absent inode-type guard on 590-603 -- `metadata.type_` is already read at line 582 and is a Metadata field (inode.rs:89), so no new plumbing is needed. Confirmed this is the only such definition: `grep 'fn check_permission' kernel/src/` returns inode.rs:573 alone, and no filesystem overrides it. Asterinas's pre-emptive subtraction (versus Linux's fallback-after-ACL-check) is *not* itself a divergence: for a DAC_OVERRIDE holder the two structures agree on every case I traced once the directory exemption is present, including non-directory 0444/0555 files.
invariant: A process holding CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE may read, write, and search a directory regardless of that directory's permission bits. The additional restriction that overriding *execute* permission requires at least one execute bit to be set in the mode applies only to non-directories.
owning_layer: VFS, above the filesystem: the default `Inode::check_permission` in kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs. This is Asterinas's exact structural counterpart to Linux's generic_permission -- it is the single definition in the tree and no filesystem overrides it, so all six filesystems inherit the rule from this one function, and the read-only-mount check sits beside it at the same level (check_mount_writable, path/mod.rs:255-262, mirroring Linux sb_permission). Patching ramfs or ext2 instead would pass statfs03 while leaving the identical defect reachable through every other filesystem, and patching the callers (check_dir_entry_mutation, resolver.rs:558) would corrupt the unprivileged half of the same test.
linux_reference: fs/namei.c generic_permission(), read verbatim at /tmp/namei.c:464-507 (provenance checked: the file carries the linux/fs/namei.c Linus/tytso header and its real do_inode_permission/sb_permission neighbours, and matches upstream including the recent no_acl_inode fast path). Structure: acl_permission_check() (380-440) runs first and only a -EACCES falls through to capabilities. Then `if (S_ISDIR(inode->i_mode))` at 476-486 -- comment `/* DACs are overridable for directories */` -- tries CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH when `!(mask & MAY_WRITE)`, then `capable_wrt_inode_uidgid(idmap, inode, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE)` returns 0 with no exec-bit test of any kind, and only then -EACCES. The condition Asterinas applies universally appears solely on the non-directory fallthrough at 496-504: `if (!(mask & MAY_EXEC) || (inode->i_mode & S_IXUGO))`. Enforcement is therefore in VFS, reached by inode_permission -> do_inode_permission, where a per-fs i_op->permission is the documented exception rather than the rule. Note: man7.org, github.com, elixir.bootlin.com and git.kernel.org were all unreachable from this container (network restricted), so the citation is the implementation rather than the man page.
other_callers: Substantial, and the target test is the mildest symptom. resolver.rs:558 lookup_at_path asks MAY_EXEC on every directory component, so root today cannot traverse into *any* directory lacking exec bits -- every path-taking syscall under a mode-0444 or mode-0600 directory returns EACCES for root where Linux succeeds. path/mod.rs:268 check_dir_entry_mutation hands the same failure to mkdir/rmdir/unlink/rename/link/symlink/create inside such a directory (this test's path). syscall/access.rs:108 mis-reports access(X_OK) on a directory for root. Genuinely unaffected, so the fix must not perturb them: path/mod.rs:743 and access.rs:102-105 (pure MAY_READ/MAY_WRITE, already subtracted at line 588); program_loader/mod.rs:124 and inode_handle.rs:46 (MAY_EXEC on regular files, where Asterinas's existing rule is already Linux's); net/socket/unix/ns/path.rs:24 and inotify.rs:95 (read/write only); and the MAY_ACCESS xattr callers ramfs/fs.rs:1354 and ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:289, since MAY_ACCESS is none of R/W/X.
suggested_direction: In the CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE branch of Inode::check_permission (inode.rs:585-604), exempt directories from the exec-bit condition: when `metadata.type_ == InodeType::Dir`, drop MAY_EXEC alongside MAY_READ|MAY_WRITE and never take the EACCES return, leaving lines 590-603 untouched for all other inode types. Do not modify check_dir_entry_mutation or resolver.rs:558 -- the MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC and MAY_EXEC they request are the same masks Linux requests, and relaxing either would break the unprivileged half of this very test, whose expected EACCES must still come from resolver.rs:558 for the nobody user. Traps for the fix phase: the assertion is an unprivileged denial, so verify both that setup now succeeds and that statfs still returns EACCES as nobody; and the effective-capability clearing on seteuid (credentials_.rs:299, set_fsuid_unchecked(new_euid) plus the setuid fixup) is what makes has_dac_override_capability false for nobody, so it must keep working. Two adjacent gaps found while reading, both out of scope and neither affecting statfs03: CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH is defined (capabilities.rs:13) and granted (credentials_.rs:341) but never consulted in check_permission, so a process holding DAC_READ_SEARCH without DAC_OVERRIDE gets no bypass at all; and has_dac_override_capability (inode.rs:631-640) omits Linux's capable_wrt_inode_uidgid requirement that the inode's uid/gid be mapped in the capability's user namespace.
